A 25-year-old male with no significant medical history seeks medical attention for lower back pain that
began the previous afternoon. The pain started immediately after lifting a heavy box from the ground,
initially presenting as sharp but now described as a dull ache. During physical examination, the L5
segment shows right sidebending and left rotation. Further examination reveals a deep left sacral
sulcus and a posterior right inferior lateral angle. What is the correct diagnosis? Answer Choices: (A)
Left on left sacral torsion (B) Posterior sacral counternutation (C) Anterior sacral nutation (D) Right
unilateral extension (E) Bilateral sacral flexion (F) Left unilateral flexion (G) Right on right sacral torsion
(H) Right on left sacral torsion (I) Bilateral sacral extension (J) Left on right sacral torsion
 A. Anterior sacral nutation
B. Bilateral sacral extension
C. Right on left sacral torsion
D. Right on right sacral torsion
E. Left unilateral flexion
F. Left on right sacral torsion
G. Posterior sacral counternutation
H. Bilateral sacral flexion
I. Left on left sacral torsion
J. Right unilateral extension
